holidays.name: National Handwriting Day
holidays.description: Dust off your favorite pen and write something by hand, like a love letter, a grocery list or a fancy signature. It's a day to enjoy cursive loops, slanted scrawls and the personal look of real handwriting in a world of keyboards.
holidays.origin: The Writing Instrument Manufacturers Association started the observance in the 1970s. They chose January 23 because it is the birthday of John Hancock, whose large signature on the Declaration of Independence is the most famous in American history.
holidays.funFact: John Hancock's signature was so big and bold that his name became a common American nickname for a person's signature.

holidays.name: International Sticky Toffee Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day for warm, gooey, caramel-drenched sponge cake. Sticky toffee pudding is a moist date-studded cake covered in toffee sauce and usually served with cream or ice cream. It's a good excuse for a second helping of dessert in the middle of winter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of Britain's best-loved comfort desserts.
holidays.funFact: The pudding has no toffee in the batter. The 'toffee' is a buttery brown sugar sauce poured over the finished cake, and the sponge gets its moisture from chopped dates.

holidays.name: Measure Your Feet Day
holidays.description: Take off your socks and get out the ruler. Today is for measuring your feet, since many people wear shoes that don't fit. It's a good time to check your size, and maybe to justify a new pair of shoes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to find their true shoe size and look after their feet.
holidays.funFact: Feet can change size over time because of age, pregnancy, weight changes and general wear. Many adults are wearing a different size than the one they bought years ago.
